title: Post-release degradation triage and telemetry escape hatch (sketch)
body:
Overview:
This is a working sketch for a focused post-release degradation triage workflow coupled with a low-friction telemetry "escape hatch" for fast mitigation. Purpose is to give on-call and release owners a compact recipe to rapidly contain user-impacting regressions (latency, error-rate, quality) without full rollback unless necessary.

Context and assumptions:
- Applies to host and dedicated model rollouts where routing and model variants can be controlled by policy (traffic steering service).
- Telemetry pipeline provides 60s and 5m aggregated signals for latency, 4xx/5xx, model-quality regression alerting (promptset scoring).
- Canary was running for at least 2 hours with low-volume sampling; this document addresses incidents that slip past canary and surface during broader rollout.

Key ideas (novel / intentionally lightweight):
- Grace-period throttles: instead of immediate rollback, throttle burst traffic to new variant for a configurable grace period (default 30m) while triage completes.
- Escape hatch: prebuilt routing policy that reroutes 100% of traffic to last-known-good model variant and disables batching/quantization changes in seconds.
- Degradation levels: define S1/S2/S3 for severity tied to automated thresholds and human review.

Preflight (release prep) checklist (short):
- Confirm routing policy for escape hatch is pre-created and owned (route-id + runbook pinned).
- Verify telemetry dashboards for the release contain: token-latency, tail-p99, error-rate by endpoint, promptset-quality delta, cache hit rate.
- Ensure canary sample promptset has baseline scores in the release notes.
- Pre-approve an on-call + release-owner pair for the 72h post-release window.
- Generate a short rollback vs throttle decision ladder and attach to release notes.

Real-time triage flow (triage steps with owners):
1) Signal detection (automated): Alert fired when one or more: latency p95 up > 30% (5m), errors > 2% absolute, promptset-score delta > 3pts.  Owner: monitoring-alerting.
2) Quick check (5m): Release owner validates the alert, looks at correlated deploy events, infra errors, and client-side changes.  Owner: release-owner.
3) Apply grace-period throttle (10m): If uncertain, apply a 50% throttle to new variant (shift 50% traffic back to previous). Deploy via routing console with the pre-made throttle policy.  Owner: traffic-ops.
4) Run targeted tests (15m): Run the canonical promptset and a short latency load focused on p90/p99. Compare against baseline.  Owner: applied-ml + qa.
5) If metrics trending back toward baseline within throttle window: keep throttled and extend grace period incremental (30m increments) and monitor.  Owner: release-owner.
6) If metrics remain bad or degrade further: trigger escape hatch -> failover to last-known-good variant.  Owner: traffic-ops + SRE.
7) Post-mitigation analysis: collect traces, sample requests, and open a postmortem ticket.  Owner: release-owner.

Escape hatch mechanics (operational runbook excerpt):
- Preconditions: route-id and previous-variant-id documented in release notes; escape policy labeled "escape-<release-id>".
- Steps: 1) Execute routing-policy swap in console to previous-variant-id (single button in console or API call: POST /routing/swap). 2) Disable any new-quantization flags in runtime via feature-flags service. 3) Reduce batching window to conservative defaults. 4) If using Dedicated nodes, warm up previous variant instances to avoid cold-penalty.
- Verification: watch p95 latency, 4xx/5xx, and promptset-quality on dashboards for 10 minutes.

Rollforward vs Rollback decision ladder (decision criteria):
- Prefer rollforward when regression is isolated, fix is small (config change, kernel selection) and can be staged in <2h with minimal risk.
- Prefer rollback (escape hatch) when core correctness is broken (generation hallucinations at scale, systemic errors, or third-party infra failure) or when the fix will take >2h and user-impact is high.
- If uncertain, prefer temporary throttle + feature-flag disable while engineering prepares a patch.

Suggested rollout calendar (compact / copyable):
- T-48h: Final go/no-go sync. Confirm telemetry and escape policy.
- T-6h: Canary tagging and canary-runbook posted.
- T+0h (release start): 10% for 15m, 25% for 30m, 50% for 30m, 100% (with grace-period throttles enabled).
- T+3h: midday check-in (release-owner) — health and promptset sanity.
- T+24h: extended monitoring review; consider A/B experiments for quality tuning.
- T+72h: release retrospective and finalize release notes.

Release notes (draft snippet to drop into the release page):
- Release id: rel-2027-06-14-77
- Summary: Optimize kernel selection for causal-decoder family and introduce a new quantization profile (q4m-lite) for medium sequences. Contains batching-window adjustments for lower tail latency.
- Notable risk items: q4m-lite may increase variance in rare token distributions; batching changes can affect p99 under long tail workloads.
- Escape policy: route-escape-rel-77 is prebuilt and tested in staging; rollback can be executed via routing console (button: "Activate escape-rel-77").
- Post-release checks: run promptset A (lead: Priya Raman) and validate quality metrics within 2%.

On-call cheat-sheet (one-liners):
- If p95 spikes >50% and errors >3%: throttle to 50% new-variant, escalate to release-owner.
- If promptset delta >5 pts: immediate escape hatch; collect 500 request samples for forensic analysis.
- If infra machine-health alerts present: open infra incident and consider rollback regardless of model metrics.

Open questions / TODOs (draft):
- Should grace-period default be 30m or 60m for high-traffic services? (action: product + SRE decision)
- Automate throttle policy application from alerts? Prototype in infra sprint. (owner: platform-engineering)
- Add a dedicated "escape-hatch dry-run" to preflight for major releases. (owner: release-engineering)

Next steps and owners:
- Finalize the decision ladder and add to release checklist (Ethan Cole).
- Implement a single-click console action for escape policies (Platform Eng).
- Run a chaos drill in July to exercise escape hatch and throttles (SRE + Release Eng).

Notes and references:
- See linked artifacts (Jira ENG-4512 for follow-up tasks).
- Reference: Confluence template for post-release triage patterns.

This is a sketch intended for use during the next rollout; please iterate and add concrete API call snippets and runbook screenshots before sign-off.
